Jera, Dell Technologies, and Rhaelm team up for behind-the-meter AI infrastructure in Japan
First project planned for power plant at Chiba
Power company Jera, Dell Technologies, and sovereign AI provider Rhaelm have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to develop AI infrastructure at a "national scale" in Japan.
Under the MoU, the three companies are developing a standardized framework for building AI infrastructure - from power and electrical infrastructure to cooling and AI compute - and will start with a behind-the-meter project in Chiba that will be backed by Apollo Global Management.
Dell will provide standardized rack-scale AI infrastructure, while Rhaelm will offer its data center development and delivery expertise, with energy provided by Jera's capabilities across LNG procurement, shipping, import and regasification, and power generation.
In Chiba, the project will be developed by Rhaelm and Jera at the latter's Chiba Thermal Power Station, located at 2-1377 Soga-cho, Chuo-ku, Chiba.
The data center will have a power capacity of up to 400MW, and will operate on a behind-the-meter basis. Operations are targeted to begin in or around 2028. An estimated $15 billion will be invested in the project across all phases of development, including land, power infrastructure, construction, and AI compute.
The liquid natural gas-powered Chiba station has a total maximum output of 4.38GW.
The companies will also look at other Jera sites for similar deployments, of which the company has more than 20, aiming to have a multi-gigawatt footprint across Japan in the 2030s.
Yukio Kani, global CEO and chair of Jera, said: "Jera is uniquely positioned to power Japan’s AI ambitions. We already generate one third of Japan’s electricity and supply nearly all of the power consumed in the Tokyo metropolitan area, with capabilities spanning the full LNG value chain, from fuel procurement, shipping, receiving terminals and gas infrastructure through to downstream power generation and reliable operations, complemented by a growing renewable energy portfolio."
Bradd Lewis, CEO & chief revenue officer, Rhaelm, added: "Rhaelm was built to solve exactly this kind of challenge, taking stranded power capacity and turning it into sovereign AI infrastructure. By co-locating at Jera's Chiba station and deploying the Dell AI Factory as our compute standard, we can deliver a 400MW facility years ahead of a conventional grid-connected timeline. Jera's behind-the-meter power and site access are the foundation, and our role is to bring the execution capability and capital to build on it, with the end goal of replicating that model across Japan at the scale the country's AI ambitions demand."
Rhaelm is an AI cloud provider headquartered in London and with operations in Europe and Asia Pacific, ultimately targeting a gigawatt-scale platform. According to its website, it has a presence in Portugal, the UK, Poland, Japan, South Korea, and Australia. The company was previously known as Sovereign AI, rebranding to Rhaelm in September.

pages.text:
JERA, Dell Technologies, and RHAELM Sign Memorandum of Understanding to Accelerate National-Scale AI Infrastructure Development in Japan
JERA Co., Inc. (hereinafter "JERA"), Dell Technologies, and RHAELM Holdings Ltd. (pronounced: Realm) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) today to formulate a basic concept and conduct business feasibility studies for developing national-scale AI infrastructure in Japan. Furthermore, as the first project under this MOU, JERA and RHAELM plan to promote AI infrastructure development at the JERA Chiba Thermal Power Station (Chiba City, Chiba Prefecture).
Based on this MOU, the three companies will jointly promote a concept (hereinafter "the Concept") to integrally standardize power generation equipment, power infrastructure, cooling equipment, and AI computing platforms to rapidly develop AI infrastructure in Japan. By integrally designing and operating everything from power generation equipment, power infrastructure, and cooling equipment to AI computing, the companies aim to resolve issues such as prolonged development periods due to individual design for each project and complex supply chains in AI infrastructure development.
https://www.jera.co.jp/news/information/20261001_2535
The background to this partnership is the expansion of AI demand in Japan, with the goal of leveraging stable gas-fired power generation and the robust LNG value chain that supports it to accelerate the development of AI infrastructure and strengthen Japan's AI competitiveness. In this Concept, the companies aim to build a new model that integrates LNG supply and AI computing by combining JERA's capabilities across the entire LNG value chain—from procurement and transport to receiving, storage, and power generation—with Dell Technologies' standardized AI infrastructure platform and RHAELM's large-scale data center development and deployment capabilities. Furthermore, the companies intend to deploy this model throughout Japan and are also considering future expansion into overseas markets.
As the first project under this Concept, JERA and RHAELM, in collaboration with Dell Technologies, will utilize a standardized model to develop AI data center infrastructure with a capacity of up to 400,000 kW at the JERA Chiba Thermal Power Station. This is currently considered the largest single-site AI deployment in Japan and one of the largest in Asia, excluding China. This project will serve as a pilot case to verify the effectiveness of the standardized model and lead to further sophistication. The companies aim to accumulate practical knowledge and operational expertise to establish a highly scalable standard model that can be deployed across Japan. The total investment is expected to exceed 15 billion USD (approximately 2.3 trillion yen) across land, power infrastructure, facility construction, and AI computing capacity, with operations targeted to begin around 2028. By receiving on-site power supply from existing power generation facilities operated by JERA, the companies aim to provide AI computing capacity several years earlier than conventional grid-connected data center developments. Additionally, JERA and RHAELM are concurrently considering the deployment of this standardized model to other thermal power stations owned by JERA in Japan, aiming to support the realization of several million kW of AI computing capacity across Japan in the 2030s.
Currently, major challenges in AI infrastructure development include engineering that requires individual design for each project, complex supply chains, and the long time required for grid connection. In Japan as well, as the role of AI in industry and society expands, the demand for AI computing capacity continues to increase. As a partner in the energy sector, JERA will take on the construction of a large-scale, always-available power supply platform necessary for AI infrastructure. By developing AI infrastructure within the premises of thermal power stations, on-site power supply from power generation equipment to AI infrastructure becomes possible, supporting the early launch and expansion of new AI infrastructure.
Dell Technologies will promote the standardization of AI computing platforms through the "Dell AI Factory," providing pre-integrated, rack-scale infrastructure that can shorten the time to deployment. RHAELM will lead the promotion of the entire project under this Concept, leveraging its expertise in the development and operation of large-scale AI infrastructure to build a highly scalable business model that enables rapid deployment across Japan by combining JERA's on-site power supply with the "Dell AI Factory." This Concept aligns with the Japanese government's policy to lead the expansion of AI computing capacity in Japan and the development of the power and digital infrastructure that forms its foundation. The three companies, under a strong partnership, will contribute to building the foundation that supports the development of Japan's AI industry.
What is the difference between on-site power supply and grid-connected power supply?
Conclusion: The biggest difference is "where the large-capacity power used by the data center (DC) is procured from." While grid-connected types procure power from the power company's transmission and distribution network, on-site types procure it directly from power generation equipment within or adjacent to the DC site.
・Supplies power to the DC from the power company's transmission and distribution network (grid)
・Utilizes existing power infrastructure: Power Plant → Transmission Line → Substation → DC
・If the existing grid does not have sufficient spare capacity, reinforcement of transmission lines, substations, etc., is required
・If grid connection and reinforcement take time, power supply must wait even after the DC is completed
・Installs power generation equipment within or adjacent to the DC site and supplies power directly to the DC
・Gas turbines, gas engines, fuel cells, etc., are the main options
・Reduces the need to secure the entire required power capacity from the grid
・Can reduce dependence on grid spare capacity and reinforcement work, potentially advancing the start of power supply
・On the other hand, construction of power generation equipment, fuel procurement, permits, etc., are required
Grid-Connected Type = "Drawing the necessary power from an external power grid"
On-Site Type = "Securing the necessary power oneself near the DC"
Since AI data centers require large-capacity power on the order of hundreds of MW to GW, grid capacity shortages often become a bottleneck for development. Therefore, the on-site type, which has the potential to secure power without waiting for grid connection, is attracting attention as a means to launch AI computing capacity early.
Why can on-site power supply provide AI computing capacity several years earlier than conventional grid-connected types?
Conclusion: This is because it avoids or shortens the 'wait for grid connection and reinforcement of large-capacity power,' which is the main bottleneck in AI data center development, allowing GPUs to be operational sooner.
・AI data centers require large-capacity power on the scale of hundreds of MW to GW.
・If the existing power grid does not have sufficient spare capacity, new construction or reinforcement of substations, transmission lines, etc., is required.
・Grid connection studies, facility reinforcement, permits, and construction can take several years, meaning that even if the DC building and GPUs are completed, they may not be able to operate due to 'waiting for power'.
・It is influenced by grid-side facility plans and other connection projects, making it difficult for DC operators alone to control the lead time.
・Install power generation equipment such as gas turbines, gas engines, or fuel cells on or adjacent to the DC site to supply power directly to the DC.
・This reduces the need to wait until the full amount of required power can be supplied from the grid.
・By proceeding with DC construction and power generation facility construction in parallel, the 'wait for power' after DC completion can be shortened.
・As a result, power supply to GPUs and full-scale operation can be brought forward, allowing AI computing capacity to be provided earlier.
Reducing dependence on grid connection and grid reinforcement
Enabling AI computing capacity to be provided several years earlier
The essence is not that 'the DC itself can be built several years earlier,' but that 'the waiting time until large-capacity power is supplied from the grid can be avoided or shortened.'
※The actual shortening period varies depending on grid spare capacity, required power amount, location, construction and permitting of on-site power generation equipment, fuel supply conditions, etc.

Susquehanna has reiterated its Positive rating on Dell Technologies (NYSE: DELL) and maintained a $700 price target.
The updated Dell price target implies approximately 28% upside from the stock’s current price of about $543, according to a September 29 analyst note.
Analyst Mehdi Hosseini pointed to growing demand for AI inferencing as a key catalyst for Dell’s server business. Susquehanna expects traditional server revenue to double in fiscal 2027 before continuing to grow at a double-digit compound annual growth rate through fiscal 2029.
According to the analyst, enterprise customers and neocloud service providers are increasing spending on computing infrastructure needed for AI inferencing applications.
This trend is expected to drive further growth across Dell’s server segment and support upside to fiscal 2028 and fiscal 2029 estimates.
Hosseini noted that inferencing is becoming an increasingly important demand driver for original equipment manufacturers such as Dell, helping sustain growth beyond the initial wave of AI training deployments.
Meanwhile, Wall Street’s broader outlook on Dell remains constructive. TradingView data shows a consensus 12-month Dell stock forecast of approximately $595, representing modest upside from current levels.
Among the more bullish projections, Susquehanna’s $700 target ranks near the top of Wall Street estimates, while some analysts have issued targets as high as $735. Current analyst ratings remain concentrated in the ‘Buy’ and ‘Strong Buy’ categories.
DELL 12-month stock price prediction. Source: TradingView
The latest analyst update follows a strong year for Dell, which has emerged as a major beneficiary of the AI infrastructure boom.
In its fiscal second-quarter 2027 results reported on September 1, Dell posted record revenue of $47 billion, up 58% year-over-year. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share came in at $7.04, representing growth of 203% from the same period last year.
AI-optimized servers remained the primary growth driver. Dell reported record AI server orders of $60.9 billion during the quarter and exited the period with a record AI backlog of $95 billion. Revenue from AI servers reached $16.4 billion, up 100% from a year earlier.
The company also raised its full-year fiscal 2027 guidance, projecting revenue of $192 billion and AI server revenue of $74 billion as AI infrastructure demand continues to accelerate.
Overall, Dell shares have delivered significant gains over the past year as investors increasingly bet on the company’s role in the expanding AI infrastructure market.
However, analysts continue to monitor AI spending trends, execution of the company’s large backlog, and broader volatility across the AI hardware sector.

Jim Cramer Prefers Dell (DELL) But Calls HPE the Cheaper Stock. Here is the Gap
Tue, October 6, 2026 at 5:17 PM PDT 4 min read
Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL) was named the better operator of the two by Jim Cramer on Mad Money on October 6, in a segment that still called Hewlett Packard Enterprise the cheaper stock.
Dell traded at around $573 on October 6, up 3.80% on the day, while Hewlett Packard Enterprise traded near $71. Cramer was precise about the trade-off. "I am not ready to say that I like HPE more than Dell because Dell's best of breed," he said, before adding that the other stock "acts a lot cheaper given the lower valuation."

Jim Cramer Prefers Dell (DELL) But Calls HPE the Cheaper Stock. Here is the Gap
The Gap Is in the Forward Multiple, Not the Trailing One:
Cramer put Dell at "18 times" earnings. The forward multiple is at around 20 times, which is close to the figure he was working from. Hewlett Packard Enterprise trades at 15.01 times forward earnings. That is the gap, and it is about five turns wide.
The trailing numbers say the opposite. Dell is at 33.33 times trailing earnings against 36.43 at Hewlett Packard Enterprise. So the cheaper stock is only cheaper on next year's estimates. On the year just finished, it is the more expensive of the two.
The entire valuation case therefore rests on forecasts rather than on results already reported. Billionaire investors hold ten semiconductor stocks. The one ranked first has returned 24% since June.

Why Dell Keeps the Operator Title:
The operating numbers explain the preference better than the multiples do. Dell grew revenue 57.70% in the most recent quarter against 33.70% at Hewlett Packard Enterprise, from a base more than three times larger.
Dell turned that into $11.38 billion of net income over the past twelve months. Hewlett Packard Enterprise earned $2.68 billion. The margins complicate it. Gross margin is 36.62% at Hewlett Packard Enterprise against 19.91% at Dell, which is the widest operating gap between them.
Yet net margin lands at 7.52% for Dell and 6.67% for its rival. A current ratio of 0.96 shows how. Dell's suppliers and customers fund the working capital, so less of the gross margin is consumed before it reaches the bottom line. One balance sheet item separates them completely. Dell carries a book value of negative $2.23 a share after years of buybacks, while Hewlett Packard Enterprise holds $19.96.
We named ten stocks for the year ahead in October. What put the first one on top is explained here.
The Valuation Case:
Dell traded at around $573 on October 6 and is worth $364.50 billion. Sustainability is the real question for both, because AI server demand is the only reason either multiple expanded.
On price, the measures disagree by design. Dell is at 2.41 times sales against 2.24 at Hewlett Packard Enterprise, which is close enough to be the same number. Enterprise value to EBITDA of 21.15 at Dell against 15.23 is the clearer separation, and it counts the $35.28 billion of debt Dell carries.
On free cash flow, the gap is wider than the multiples suggest. Dell yields 2.3% of its market value in free cash against 4.4% at Hewlett Packard Enterprise, which is the cheapness Cramer is pointing at without needing anyone's forecast.
Conclusion:
Cramer is making a quality argument and a price argument at the same time, and they point in opposite directions. Dell grew quarterly revenue 57.70% and earned $11.38 billion against $2.68 billion, which is the operator case. However, the cheaper label only holds on forward estimates at 15.01 times against 19.69. On trailing earnings, Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the more expensive stock at 36.43 times. The number to watch is gross margin, because 19.91% at Dell is what the better operator has to keep defending.

Management framed this as proof of its engineering and deployment strength, as well as global support capabilities, reinforcing Dell’s strategic position in next-generation AI data-center architectures.
Exceptional Traditional Server Growth and Share Gains
Beyond GPUs, traditional server and networking revenue jumped 122% to $10.5 billion, fueled by data-center modernization, consolidation and rising CPU demand for AI and agentic workloads. Dell said it gained more than 10 percentage points of server share over the past two quarters and expects further share gains in the current quarter.
Durable Server Refresh Cycle Still Ahead
The company sees a long runway in server refresh, noting that 1.2 million assets in its installed base are 14th generation or older. Dell expects continued modernization into 17th- and 18th-generation platforms, with 18th-generation servers set to begin shipping next month, supporting sustained infrastructure demand.
Storage Returns to Growth with Market Share Wins
Storage is back in growth mode, with revenue up 26% to $4.9 billion and demand for Dell IP products outpacing the market for six consecutive quarters. PowerStore delivered double-digit demand growth for the ninth straight quarter, contributing to improved storage profitability and ongoing share gains.
Broad Storage Portfolio Shows Strong Momentum
Dell’s full storage stack is firing, as PowerFlex, PowerStore, PowerProtect and PowerVault all posted strong growth during the quarter. Unstructured storage, led by PowerScale and ObjectScale, delivered another exceptional period, marking three straight quarters of double-digit or better growth, alongside strength in Data Domain and all-flash arrays.
AI Drives New Storage Use Cases and Demand
Management described early but growing storage demand tied directly to AI workloads, as customers manage and protect larger data volumes. New use cases include agent-created files, logs, traces, KV cache and data from physical AI, manufacturing, IoT sensors and robotics, creating incremental opportunities across the portfolio.
Client Solutions Group Delivers Solid Growth
The PC and device business remained resilient, with Client Solutions Group revenue up 20% to $15 billion overall. Commercial revenue climbed 22% to $13.2 billion, marking the eighth consecutive growth quarter, while consumer revenue rose 7% to $1.8 billion, the fourth straight quarter of demand growth.
CSG Profitability Supports Scale and Cash Generation
CSG delivered operating income of $1.1 billion, or 7.6% of revenue, aided by pricing discipline and scale efficiencies. Dell emphasized that CSG is a capital-efficient cash engine that underpins its supply chain, broad portfolio, growth investments and robust shareholder-return program.
Record Cash Flow and Shareholder Capital Returns
Cash flow from operations reached $2.2 billion in the quarter, while adjusted free cash flow hit a record $8.1 billion. Dell returned a record $4.3 billion to shareholders, repurchasing 9.5 million shares at an average price of $401 and distributing a cash dividend, demonstrating confidence in future earnings power.
Healthy Balance Sheet and Improving Credit Profile
The company closed the quarter with $14.2 billion in cash and investments, up $0.2 billion sequentially, and a core leverage ratio of 0.8x. Management pointed to positive credit-rating actions and said strong cash generation and a solid balance sheet give Dell flexibility to invest while continuing to return capital.
Strong First Half Underscores Growth Inflection
Across the first two quarters, revenue reached $90.8 billion, up 71%, while EPS rose 208% to $11.90, underscoring the magnitude of this cycle. Cash flow from operations and shareholder returns both hit record levels at $6.3 billion, setting a high bar for the balance of the fiscal year.
Ongoing Investment in Infrastructure Capabilities
To sustain momentum, Dell is investing heavily in AI platforms, engineering expertise and global deployment capabilities. It is also expanding supply-chain capacity, data-management tools and a data automation platform designed to support increasingly complex AI and data workloads across its customer base.
Supply Constraints Across Key Components
Management cautioned that demand is outstripping supply, leaving Dell constrained on critical components, especially DRAM and NAND. Additional bottlenecks include CPUs, disk drives, leading- and mature-node products, ABF substrate, T-Glass and optical parts, all of which could limit near-term shipment upside.
Customer Orders Delayed by Product Availability
Some large customers want products faster than Dell can currently deliver, leading to deferrals of certain purchases. In response, buyers are placing orders earlier to secure access to constrained supply, extending visibility but also highlighting the operational challenges of meeting AI-related demand.
While CSG remains profitable, Dell expects operating income rate to ease to about 6% in Q3, as it balances growth and share against pricing. Management also flagged a competitive PC landscape and noted that unit volumes are likely to be down in the second half, prompting ongoing price discovery.
Higher Variable Compensation Lifts Operating Expenses
Operating expenses increased 22% to $4 billion, with management attributing much of the rise to higher variable compensation tied to strong company performance. Even so, opex fell meaningfully as a percentage of revenue, reinforcing the underlying operating leverage of the model.
Pricing and Input-Cost Inflation in Infrastructure
Growth in traditional servers and storage includes a meaningful contribution from price increases as component costs move higher. Storage pricing in particular reflects higher material costs, especially NAND, suggesting that part of the revenue surge is driven by inflation in the supply chain.
Lightning Product Still Early in Commercial Cycle
Dell’s Lightning parallel file-system offering remains in an early commercialization phase, currently in beta with several customers. The product is in competitive runoffs, and management framed it as a strategic bet for high-performance AI and data workloads rather than a near-term revenue driver.
Management noted that more cost-sensitive customers are stretching PC upgrade timelines, resulting in a larger installed base of older devices. While commercial demand is healthy, these extended cycles could temper consumer growth and require continued product and pricing adjustments.
Robust Guidance Signals Confidence in AI Upside
For Q3, Dell guided to $49 billion in revenue at the midpoint, up roughly 80% year on year, with ISG up about 145% and AI server revenue at $19 billion. Full-year guidance calls for $192 billion in revenue, about 70% growth, EPS of $25.50, AI server revenue tripling to $74 billion and operating expenses held near 8% of revenue as operating income grows roughly 120%.
Dell’s earnings call painted the picture of a company firmly in the slipstream of the AI infrastructure boom, while still capitalizing on a steady PC recovery. Despite supply bottlenecks, margin normalization in CSG and rising input costs, management’s confidence and sharply raised guidance suggest investors are looking at a multi-year growth story rather than a fleeting spike in demand.

By Trader EdgeSeptember 29, 2026No Comments4 Mins Read
TD Cowen elevated Dell’s (DELL) price target from $500 to $550 while maintaining a Hold rating.
Susquehanna maintains a Positive outlook with a $700 price target, highlighting AI inferencing as a significant growth driver.
The company reports a $95 billion AI server backlog, with the majority being noncancelable orders.
Truist Securities increased its price target to $505, while RBC Capital initiated coverage with an Outperform rating.
InvestingPro data reveals Dell achieved 49% revenue expansion over the previous year, fueled by AI demand.
Shares of Dell Technologies (DELL) stock hovered near $543.95 during Tuesday’s trading session, registering a modest 0.10% increase. The price movement followed a wave of analyst upgrades released throughout the week.
TD Cowen increased its price objective for Dell shares to $550, up from the previous $500 mark. Analyst Krish Sankar maintained a Hold rating alongside the revised target.
The adjustment came after recent discussions with Paul Frantz, Dell’s head of investor relations. Sankar noted that Dell’s AI server order backlog has reached $95 billion, with the bulk consisting of noncancelable commitments.
This substantial backlog provides Dell with significant negotiating power among leading neocloud service providers. Sankar indicated that order patterns during the latter half of 2026 will be critical for assessing potential upside in 2027 AI projections.
Sankar also highlighted profitability considerations. An increased proportion of AI CPU rack configurations would enhance margins, given Dell’s current gross margin of approximately 20%.
Massive AI Pipeline Drives Positive Analyst Sentiment
Susquehanna’s Mehdi Hosseini echoed a bullish perspective. He maintained a Positive rating on Dell shares while reaffirming his $700 price objective.
Hosseini suggested that expanding AI inferencing requirements could provide substantial momentum for Dell’s conventional server operations. His projections anticipate traditional server revenue will double during fiscal 2027 and maintain double-digit growth rates through fiscal 2029.
He believes Dell may surpass the 100% year-over-year growth guidance already provided by management for fiscal 2027. Hosseini attributes this optimism to emerging agentic AI applications and increasing CPU requirements.
Hosseini provided detailed calculations in his analysis. He projects approximately $0.10 in traditional server revenue for each $1 of accelerated compute revenue from neocloud clients, and $0.23 per dollar for enterprise customers.
When applied to Dell’s $74 billion AI server revenue projection for fiscal 2027, this formula suggests roughly $7 billion in associated traditional compute requirements. That represents a modest portion of the estimated $40 billion traditional server revenue anticipated for the year, with inferencing accounting for approximately 18%.
Hosseini anticipates this percentage will exceed 20% during fiscal 2028 and 2029. He contends the broader market opportunity remains undervalued beyond the fiscal 2027 timeframe.
TD Cowen wasn’t alone in adjusting its forecast this week. Truist Securities lifted its Dell price objective to $505, emphasizing a backlog that provides revenue visibility extending into fiscal 2028.
RBC Capital launched coverage on Dell with an Outperform designation. The firm highlighted Dell’s strategic positioning within AI infrastructure investment as a primary catalyst.
Goldman Sachs also identified Dell among several technology enterprises experiencing tangible financial benefits from AI implementations. The firm noted these advantages are expanding into revenue-producing operations, beyond mere capital expenditure.
Regarding potential challenges, Sankar identified memory supply limitations in 2027 as a factor requiring monitoring. He also mentioned Dell’s client solutions division confronts near-term and medium-term pressures as IT budgets reallocate from personal computers toward infrastructure investments.
InvestingPro data indicates 22 analysts have upgraded their earnings projections for Dell’s upcoming reporting period. However, InvestingPro’s Fair Value analysis suggests the stock may be valued above its calculated intrinsic worth at present price levels.
Two Dell subsidiaries recently finalized a $5 billion senior unsecured notes issuance. The offering comprised multiple tranches featuring varying maturity dates and interest rates.

Dell Technologies Introduces New Pro Rugged Laptops
Dell Technologies (NYSE: DELL) announces two new rugged laptops, Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14, purpose-built for field workers who need technology that performs in the harshest conditions. From utility technicians troubleshooting infrastructure in extreme weather to public safety officers coordinating response efforts in the field, both devices are designed to keep workers productive when conditions are most demanding.
Managing a fleet of devices across distributed field operations demands technology that won't let workers down. Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 give IT teams a standardized, manageable platform that combines field-grade durability, AI-ready performance and advanced connectivity for large-scale field deployments.
Designed for workers across federal and local government, public safety, manufacturing, oil and gas, transportation and utilities, Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 are built to perform in the most demanding conditions. They are MIL-STD-810H certified for proven reliability with a temperature range of -20°F to 145°F, covering virtually any climate field workers might face. Displays feature gloved and water multitouch support for use in personal protective equipment or wet conditions.
Both laptops are powered by Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processors that offload AI and background tasks, keeping the system responsive during long shifts. They offer optional private 5G, Wi-Fi 7 and GPS for reliable connectivity and location tracking in remote locations. Hot-swappable batteries help ensure uninterrupted productivity for even the longest shifts. With up to a 5MP RGB+IR camera available on both laptops, workers can capture high-quality images and video in any environment.
Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 are equipped with Rugged Control Center, built-in software that makes critical device settings easily accessible. From GPS module configuration to custom hardware shortcuts and device customization, it gives field workers the control they need to tailor their devices to the demands of the job.
Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme: Maximum durability in the smallest footprint
Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme is the most powerful and smallest 13-inch fully rugged AI PC. Built for the harshest environments, it carries an IP66 rating for full protection against dust and water ingress and has been drop-tested from six feet.
Performance: Intel Arc integrated graphics support visual and data-heavy workflows and up to 64 GB of LPDDR5X memory offers responsive performance for heavy multitasking. Removable SSD and self-encrypting drive options give organizations control over security and compliance in sensitive environments.
Display experience: The 13.3-inch FHD display reaches 1,400 nits of brightness for full readability in direct sunlight.
Dell Pro Rugged 14: Professional-grade performance for field work
Dell Pro Rugged 14 is built for professionals who need advanced performance in a portable, field-ready form factor. It's the smallest and most powerful 14-inch semi-rugged AI PC, weighing approximately 4.7 pounds, yet durable enough for field work with three-foot drop protection and an IP-53 rating for protection against dust, dirt and water exposure.
Performance: With an NVIDIA RTX PRO 500 Blackwell Generation Laptop GPU, users can support demanding visualization, data analysis and AI workloads in the field. LPCAMM2 memory up to 64 GB makes it easier for IT teams to upgrade or swap memory modules.
Display experience: The 14-inch 16:10 FHD display delivers up to 1,100 nits of brightness with a wider aspect ratio for reviewing documents, data dashboards and field applications.
Vehicle docking: Redesigned vehicle docking with quad passthrough provides enhanced connectivity and compatibility with third-party docking solutions, and an improved user experience makes it easy to dock and undock, ideal for workers who operate primarily from the road.
New Dell Pro Rugged laptops include Trusted Platform Module (TPM) 2.0, contacted and contactless smart card readers, fingerprint readers and IR cameras for Windows Hello facial recognition. Dell SafeID with ControlVault and BIOS-level defenses make these laptops the world's most secure rugged PCs, now further hardened with quantum-resistant protections. For IT teams managing large fleets, the laptops support cloud-based deployment, management and security tools, backed by Dell ProSupport and predictive maintenance tools to minimize downtime.
Charlie Walker"Field workers keep critical operations running no matter the conditions, and their technology needs to do the same. Our new Dell Pro Rugged laptops deliver the performance, durability and connectivity that keep workers productive when it matters most, with the standardization and security IT teams need for small to large-scale deployments."
Dell Pro Rugged 13 Extreme and Dell Pro Rugged 14 will be available in early October.

Tue, October 6, 2026 at 6:40 AM PDT 5 min read
Dell Technologies DELL shares have jumped 32.4% in the past three months, outperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's rise of 9.2%. The appreciation can be attributed to a combination of accelerating AI infrastructure demand, a broader data-center refresh cycle, improving profitability and a sharply higher fiscal 2027 outlook.
Year to date (YTD), DELL stock has jumped 338.7%, outperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's rise of 25.5%. DELL has also outperformed Super Micro Computer SMCI, Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE and HP HPQ, shares of which have returned 47.5%, 184.6% and 41.2%, respectively, over the same time frame. So, what should investors do with DELL stock? Let's find out.
DELL is benefiting from strong demand for AI-optimized infrastructure. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, AI server orders reached a record $60.9 billion, while revenues were $16.4 billion and ending backlog climbed to $95 billion. Importantly, demand is becoming more diversified. The AI customer base surpassed 6,500 across neocloud, sovereign and enterprise customers in the second quarter of fiscal 2027. Customers are replacing aging infrastructure to improve processing capacity, power efficiency, security and resiliency. A majority of Dell's installed base remains on 13th-generation or older servers, providing a sizeable multi-year refresh opportunity.
DELL has stated that AI bookings totaled roughly $132 billion over the trailing 12 months and highlighted that enterprise AI adoption is growing the fastest on a percentage basis. Dell believes enterprises remain early in the adoption cycle, with only around 10-15% having undertaken meaningful AI or agentic modernization. This leaves substantial room for additional infrastructure deployment. Dell expects fiscal 2027 AI server revenues of $74 billion, roughly three times the prior-year level.
Dell's ability to deploy complex AI clusters quickly is becoming an additional competitive differentiator. Dell's scale, longstanding supplier relationships and ability to redirect components across its broad portfolio provide an advantage in obtaining and allocating scarce components.

Dell Technologies Turns Enterprise Data Into Trusted Context for AI Agents
Tue, October 6, 2026 at 6:00 AM PDT 7 min read
Dell AI Data Platform, the data foundation of the Dell AI Factory, expands with new data orchestration and storage capabilities
Unified Semantic Layer and Enterprise Knowledge Graph give every application and agent the same trusted view of enterprise data
Dell AI Data Platform shortens the wait between question and insight with accelerated data processing that processes data nearly 4 times faster on average than CPUs alone
Dell AI Data Platform storage enhancements improve security and benchmark performance
New AI-ready data services move organizations from deployment to production quickly and reliably
ROUND ROCK, Texas, October 06, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Dell Technologies (NYSE: DELL) expands the Dell AI Data Platform so AI systems deliver better answers, cost less to run and reach production faster, giving applications and agents trusted, current context from a company's own data.
In most cases the model isn't the bottleneck to achieving enterprise scale for AI. The data is. A company's most useful information sits in files, databases, cloud services and systems across multiple sites. Most of it was created long before anyone expected an AI agent to read it. It was never labeled, connected or organized with a machine reader in mind. As a result, agents burn tokens reconstructing answers that should already exist. Every query means more steps, more compute, more cost and slower, less trustworthy results.
The Dell AI Data Platform is built end to end, from where data is stored to where agents use it. Storage moves critical data to accelerated compute without bottlenecks; orchestration connects and prepares it; analytics and search transform and index it. NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models enable document parsing, embedding and reranking. NVIDIA cuVS accelerates vector indexing and search. Because every layer runs on one platform, everything it produces traces back to governed data the customer already owns. Agents return to the same documents, history and decisions repeatedly, and most systems rebuild their understanding from scratch every time. That means answering the same two questions on every request: what does this term mean and how does it relate to everything else? Dell is extending the Dell AI Data Platform with three new features to answer both at once.
The Unified Semantic Layer gives structured and unstructured information consistent business meaning with rules, definitions and a searchable glossary, so a term means the same thing everywhere it appears. If one system calls it a client and another calls it an account, AI now knows they're the same thing. Users can also import existing ontologies and classification taxonomies, reusing industry-standard or enterprise-specific taxonomy assets. Dell is also enabling NVIDIA Auto-Ontology, an open-source library that builds knowledge graphs from enterprise data, to extend the Unified Semantic Layer.
The Enterprise Knowledge Graph maps how structured and unstructured data is related, so an application or an agent can find the right context. It uses metadata, lineage and query history to keep tuning the graph as activity changes. When an agent asks a question, the platform pulls in every related piece it's allowed to see: the right tables, data products, multimodal data and vector indexes, wherever they live. For instance, a manufacturer chasing a production line problem can trace one odd sensor reading to the machine, its repair history, the supplier batch and the orders at risk.
Knowledge Agents put that context to work. Each one acts as a trusted advisor on a single topic, grounded in a defined slice of the Enterprise Knowledge Graph. Customers set the rules: what guidance it follows, what data it can see, what quality bar it must clear and how much it's allowed to spend. NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models provide reasoning and visual understanding to Knowledge Agents.
The Unified Semantic Layer, Knowledge Graph and Knowledge Agents hold a customer's most valuable and sensitive information, so they stay inside the platform in the customer's data center. The platform builds context from that data, keeps it current as the business changes and shares it across every application and agent, without locking customers into any single model, data or storage provider.
Acceleration and security built into the data path
Business context is only reliable if data is accurate, current and governed from source to application. Customers should not have to adopt another proprietary layer to accelerate different parts of their data environment. Dell brings acceleration into the data engines themselves, working with NVIDIA across the data path. Data must be transformed and analyzed, then reach accelerated compute fast enough to keep GPUs saturated and stay protected along the way. Dell data and storage advancements include:
cuDF accelerated data processing with Apache Arrow: New testing shows that the Dell Data Processing Engine, powered by NVIDIA cuDF on NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, processes data nearly 4 times faster on average than CPUs alone across a range of workloads, and up to 20 times faster on batch processing workloads.¹ Apache Arrow moves data efficiently between Dell storage and processing, so jobs can query data in place. This can reduce data-preparation time and shorten the path from raw enterprise information to trusted context.
Expanded multitenancy and security: Dell PowerScale now supports up to 500 tenants in a single cluster, with mTLS over NFS to encrypt and authenticate file traffic and more granular role-based access control for managing each tenant. AI service providers and enterprises running shared AI platforms can serve more teams and customers from one cluster while keeping each tenant's data isolated and secure.
Benchmark workload performance: The new Dell Storage Performance Tool helps customers confidently size AI infrastructure, compare vendor solutions and keep GPUs fed by testing the performance of their S3-compatible object storage across training, inference and checkpointing.
Dell is expanding Dell AI Data Platform implementation services across its data and storage engines to move organizations from deployment to production results quickly and reliably. Dell Services establish a production-ready foundation, activating the platform's analytics, processing, search and orchestration capabilities while keeping the platform tuned to the demands of AI workloads.
Arthur Lewis, president, Infrastructure Solutions Group, Dell Technologies:
"Data without context is just noise. Most enterprises have spent years making their data accessible. That's not the same as making it usable. An agent that can find a customer record but doesn't know what it means, how it connects to everything else, or whether it can be trusted isn't intelligent. It's just fast. The companies that solve it won't just deploy AI faster or run more agents. They'll get more out of the data they already have."

Why Is Dell Technologies (DELL) Up 9.3% Since Last Earnings Report?
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 7:30 AM PDT 5 min read
A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Dell Technologies (DELL). Shares have added about 9.3% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.
Will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Dell Technologies due for a pullback? Well, first let's take a quick look at its most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent drivers for Dell Technologies Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.
DELL Q2 Earnings Beat Estimates, Strong AI Demand Aids Revenue Growth
Dell Technologies reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $7.04 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 41.65%. The company reported earnings of $2.32 per share in the year-ago quarter.
Revenues surged 58% to $46.97 billion and beat the consensus mark by 8.57%. Broad-based infrastructure demand drove the quarterly results, while AI server orders reached a record $60.9 billion.
DELL's ISG Growth Accelerates Across the Portfolio
Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) revenues jumped 89% year over year to a record $31.78 billion. AI-optimized server revenues doubled to $16.4 billion, while traditional servers and networking revenues surged 122% year over year to $10.53 billion. Dell exited the quarter with $95 billion of AI backlog, while its opportunity pipeline remained multiples of backlog.
Storage revenues increased 26% year over year to $4.85 billion as Dell IP demand grew above the market for a sixth consecutive quarter.
ISG operating income jumped 225% year over year to $4.78 billion, with operating margin expanding 620 basis points (bps) on a year-over-year basis to 15%. Dell also said its AI customer base surpassed 6,500 across neocloud, sovereign and enterprise customers.
Dell's Server Refresh Opportunity Supports Demand
Dell said traditional server demand reflects data-center modernization, security and resiliency requirements, and rising CPU needs tied to AI and agentic workloads. The company still has roughly 1.2 million installed assets running 14th-generation or older servers, leaving a sizable refresh opportunity as customers upgrade infrastructure.
Dell also highlighted significant consolidation benefits from newer systems. Seventeenth-generation servers can replace five to seven legacy servers, while 18th-generation systems can replace up to 13. The newer platforms also offer higher processing density and better power efficiency, supporting modernization even as industry supply remains constrained.
Dell's CSG Posts Broad-Based Revenue Growth
Client Solutions Group (CSG) revenues increased 20% year over year to $15.03 billion. Commercial revenues rose 22% year over year to $13.19 billion, marking the eighth straight quarter of growth, while consumer revenues advanced 7% to $1.84 billion. Demand grew across all regions and verticals, led by large-enterprise PC refresh activity.
CSG operating income increased 42% year over year to $1.14 billion. The operating margin improved 120 bps to 7.6%, supported by pricing discipline and greater scale.
Dell said it will continue balancing demand with product availability as it pursues profitable share gains in the client business.
DELL Expands Profitability Through Scale and Mix
Non-GAAP gross margin rose 78% year over year to $9.93 billion, while the gross margin improved to 21.1% from 18.7%.
Non-GAAP operating expenses increased 22% year over year to $4 billion but fell to 8.5% of revenues from 11% a year earlier, reflecting meaningful operating leverage.
That expense leverage helped non-GAAP operating income surge 160% year over year to $5.93 billion. The operating margin expanded to 12.6% from 7.7%, aided by higher revenue scale, pricing discipline and improved storage profitability.
Management tied part of the storage improvement to a higher mix of Dell IP products and better rates across solutions.
DELL Delivers Strong Cash Flow and Capital Returns
As of July 31, 2026, DELL has $14.248 billion in cash and investments and a core leverage ratio of 0.8 times. The company reported $14.062 billion in cash and investments as of May 1.
Cash flow from operations totaled $2.23 billion in the reported quarter, while adjusted free cash flow reached $8.15 billion.
Dell returned a record $4.3 billion to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends, underscoring the cash generation from higher profitability and revenue scale. Dell repurchased 9.5 million shares at an average price of $401 per share and paid a quarterly dividend of about 63 cents per share.
Dell Raises Fiscal 2027 Revenue and Earnings Outlook
For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, Dell expects revenues of $49 billion, plus or minus $500 million, and non-GAAP earnings of $6.50 per share, plus or minus 10 cents.
DELL expects ISG revenues to grow roughly 145%, supported by about $19 billion in AI server revenues, while CSG revenues are expected to rise roughly 15%.
For fiscal 2027, Dell raised its revenue outlook by $25 billion to $192 billion, plus or minus $2 billion, and lifted non-GAAP earnings guidance to $25.50 per share, plus or minus 25 cents.
AI server revenues are now expected to reach $74 billion, or roughly three times the prior-year level, with traditional server growth forecast at just over 100%.
How Have Estimates Been Moving Since Then?
It turns out, fresh estimates have trended upward during the past month.
The consensus estimate has shifted 48.54% due to these changes.
Currently, Dell Technologies has a average Growth Score of C, a score with the same score on the momentum front. Charting a somewhat similar path, the stock was allocated a score of D on the value side, putting it in the bottom 40% for this investment strategy.
Overall, the stock has an aggregate VGM Score of C. If you aren't focused on one strategy, this score is the one you should be interested in.
Estimates have been trending upward for the stock, and the magnitude of these revisions looks promising. It comes with little surprise Dell Technologies has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). We expect an above average return from the stock in the next few months.

Dell Technologies (DELL) Raises its AI Server Forecast for the Second Time This Year
On September 1, CNBC reported that Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL) shares surged 9% after the firm raised its fiscal 2027 profit and revenue outlook for the second time this year due to surging AI server demand.
Dell now expects $25.50 in adjusted earnings per share on $192 billion in revenue, up from a May outlook of $17.90 per share and $165 billion to $169 billion, and well above analyst estimates of $18.92 per share and $172.67 billion. Dell raised its fiscal 2027 AI-optimized server revenue forecast to $74 billion, up from $60 billion and more than triple the $25 billion it shipped in fiscal 2026. Second-quarter revenue hit a record $47 billion, up 58% year over year and above the $44.92 billion estimate, with adjusted EPS of $7.04 versus a $4.91 estimate. AI server orders reached a record $60.9 billion in the quarter. It pushed Dell's backlog to $95 billion, more than double the $43 billion it reported at the end of fiscal 2026. Dell's AI customer base has passed 6,500, with 3,300 added over the past three quarters.
Dell Technologies (DELL) Raises Its AI Server Forecast for the Second Time This Year
The results crushed already raised expectations across every major metric. Revenue beat estimates by more than $2 billion, and adjusted EPS beat estimates by more than $2 per share. Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL) also raised its guidance for the second time this year, and its full-year EPS guidance now stands 35% above analysts' pre-report expectations.
The backlog points to strong forward demand visibility, not just a strong quarter. Dell's $95 billion order backlog more than doubled in just two quarters, while its AI customer base expanded beyond 6,500 accounts across neoclouds, sovereign buyers, and large enterprises. This customer base reduces Dell's dependence on any single large customer.
Growth extends well beyond AI servers since Dell's Infrastructure Solutions Group generated $31.8 billion in revenue, up 89% year over year. The results show that a broader server refresh cycle and data-center modernization wave also back up Dell's traditional infrastructure business alongside the AI boom.
Dell is funding this growth while returning cash to shareholders. The company returned $4.3 billion through buybacks and dividends this quarter. Executives also pointed to recent price increases as a source of pricing power that supports the higher revenue outlook. This combination gives Dell another growth lever beyond higher shipment volumes.
The massive backlog represents future orders, not booked revenue. Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL) has not disclosed a schedule for converting the $95 billion backlog into actual sales. Hence, investors must watch the timing of that conversion to determine whether Dell can meet its guidance on schedule.
Part of the higher outlook reflects cost inflation rather than pure demand growth. Dell's chief operating officer said the firm included price increases tied to rising input costs in its higher revenue guidance. Investors therefore must determine whether Dell can protect margins as AI-server competition intensifies and component costs fluctuate.
Dell also relies heavily on Nvidia's chips and competes directly with Super Micro Computer for cloud-provider customers. This reliance exposes Dell to supply-chain constraints and competitive pressure across AI infrastructure. So a slowdown in AI infrastructure spending could put significant pressure on Dell's growth line.
Insider Monkey's database shows Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL) was held by 77 hedge funds in the second quarter of 2026, up from 72 in the first quarter. Super Micro Computer, a smaller but closely watched AI server rival, saw even sharper growth, with the fund count rising to 62 from 49.
Dell's strong results and growing AI business give investors a compelling growth story. However, the company still needs to convert its massive backlog into revenue while managing rising costs and intense AI-server competition. Therefore, investors should watch whether Dell can sustain its momentum and turn strong AI demand into durable growth.

The Gap Is in the Forward Multiple, Not the Trailing One:
Cramer put Dell at "18 times" earnings. The forward multiple is at around 20 times, which is close to the figure he was working from. Hewlett Packard Enterprise trades at 15.01 times forward earnings. That is the gap, and it is about five turns wide.
The trailing numbers say the opposite. Dell is at 33.33 times trailing earnings against 36.43 at Hewlett Packard Enterprise. So the cheaper stock is only cheaper on next year's estimates. On the year just finished, it is the more expensive of the two.
The entire valuation case therefore rests on forecasts rather than on results already reported. Billionaire investors hold ten semiconductor stocks. The one ranked first has returned 24% since June.

Why Dell Keeps the Operator Title:
The operating numbers explain the preference better than the multiples do. Dell grew revenue 57.70% in the most recent quarter against 33.70% at Hewlett Packard Enterprise, from a base more than three times larger.
Dell turned that into $11.38 billion of net income over the past twelve months. Hewlett Packard Enterprise earned $2.68 billion. The margins complicate it. Gross margin is 36.62% at Hewlett Packard Enterprise against 19.91% at Dell, which is the widest operating gap between them.

Cramer is making a quality argument and a price argument at the same time, and they point in opposite directions. Dell grew quarterly revenue 57.70% and earned $11.38 billion against $2.68 billion, which is the operator case. Dell Technologies Earnings Call Highlights AI Supercycle
Tipranks - Tipranks - Wed Sep 16, 7:38PM CDT
Dell Technologies ((DELL)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.
Dell Technologies’ latest earnings call struck a decidedly upbeat tone, with management emphasizing record results across revenue, earnings, AI orders, backlog, cash flow and shareholder returns. While executives acknowledged supply constraints, rising component costs and pockets of demand softness, the message was clear that AI-driven infrastructure and a revitalized PC business are powering a major upcycle for the company.
Record-Breaking Revenue and Earnings Performance
Fiscal Q2 marked a landmark quarter for Dell, as revenue surged 58% year over year to a record $47 billion, reflecting broad-based strength across infrastructure and PCs. Diluted earnings per share jumped 203% to a record $7.04, underscoring how rapidly the firm is converting top-line momentum into bottom-line growth.
Powerful Operating Leverage Boosts Profitability
Profitability expanded sharply, with gross margin dollars up 78% to $9.9 billion and operating income up 160% to $5.9 billion, driving net income growth of 189% to $4.6 billion. Operating expenses rose 22% to $4 billion, yet fell to 8.5% of revenue, showing strong scale benefits and tight cost control as the business grows.
AI Engine: Record Orders, Revenue and Backlog
AI infrastructure has become Dell’s primary growth engine, with quarterly AI server orders hitting $60.9 billion and AI server revenue reaching $16.4 billion. Ending AI backlog climbed to a record $95 billion, and the company booked $131.7 billion of AI server orders over the past 12 months, with pipeline levels still multiples of backlog.
The Dell AI Factory platform is scaling quickly, with customer count surpassing 6,500 and 3,300 added in just three quarters. Demand is broadening across Neoclouds, sovereign entities, enterprises and high-frequency trading firms, while enterprise customers, repeat buyers and pipeline all grew both quarter over quarter and year over year.
First to Ship NVIDIA Vera Rubin Rack Systems
Dell highlighted its innovation edge by becoming the first company to ship rack systems built on the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform. Management framed this as proof of its engineering and deployment strength, as well as global support capabilities, reinforcing Dell’s strategic position in next-generation AI data-center architectures.
Exceptional Traditional Server Growth and Share Gains
Beyond GPUs, traditional server and networking revenue jumped 122% to $10.5 billion, fueled by data-center modernization, consolidation and rising CPU demand for AI and agentic workloads. Dell said it gained more than 10 percentage points of server share over the past two quarters and expects further share gains in the current quarter.
Durable Server Refresh Cycle Still Ahead
The company sees a long runway in server refresh, noting that 1.2 million assets in its installed base are 14th generation or older. Dell expects continued modernization into 17th- and 18th-generation platforms, with 18th-generation servers set to begin shipping next month, supporting sustained infrastructure demand.
Storage Returns to Growth with Market Share Wins
Storage is back in growth mode, with revenue up 26% to $4.9 billion and demand for Dell IP products outpacing the market for six consecutive quarters. PowerStore delivered double-digit demand growth for the ninth straight quarter, contributing to improved storage profitability and ongoing share gains.
Broad Storage Portfolio Shows Strong Momentum
Dell’s full storage stack is firing, as PowerFlex, PowerStore, PowerProtect and PowerVault all posted strong growth during the quarter. Unstructured storage, led by PowerScale and ObjectScale, delivered another exceptional period, marking three straight quarters of double-digit or better growth, alongside strength in Data Domain and all-flash arrays.
AI Drives New Storage Use Cases and Demand
Management described early but growing storage demand tied directly to AI workloads, as customers manage and protect larger data volumes. New use cases include agent-created files, logs, traces, KV cache and data from physical AI, manufacturing, IoT sensors and robotics, creating incremental opportunities across the portfolio.
Client Solutions Group Delivers Solid Growth
The PC and device business remained resilient, with Client Solutions Group revenue up 20% to $15 billion overall. Commercial revenue climbed 22% to $13.2 billion, marking the eighth consecutive growth quarter, while consumer revenue rose 7% to $1.8 billion, the fourth straight quarter of demand growth.
CSG Profitability Supports Scale and Cash Generation
CSG delivered operating income of $1.1 billion, or 7.6% of revenue, aided by pricing discipline and scale efficiencies. Dell emphasized that CSG is a capital-efficient cash engine that underpins its supply chain, broad portfolio, growth investments and robust shareholder-return program.
Record Cash Flow and Shareholder Capital Returns
Cash flow from operations reached $2.2 billion in the quarter, while adjusted free cash flow hit a record $8.1 billion. Dell returned a record $4.3 billion to shareholders, repurchasing 9.5 million shares at an average price of $401 and distributing a cash dividend, demonstrating confidence in future earnings power.
Healthy Balance Sheet and Improving Credit Profile
The company closed the quarter with $14.2 billion in cash and investments, up $0.2 billion sequentially, and a core leverage ratio of 0.8x. Management pointed to positive credit-rating actions and said strong cash generation and a solid balance sheet give Dell flexibility to invest while continuing to return capital.
Strong First Half Underscores Growth Inflection
Across the first two quarters, revenue reached $90.8 billion, up 71%, while EPS rose 208% to $11.90, underscoring the magnitude of this cycle. Cash flow from operations and shareholder returns both hit record levels at $6.3 billion, setting a high bar for the balance of the fiscal year.
Ongoing Investment in Infrastructure Capabilities
To sustain momentum, Dell is investing heavily in AI platforms, engineering expertise and global deployment capabilities. It is also expanding supply-chain capacity, data-management tools and a data automation platform designed to support increasingly complex AI and data workloads across its customer base.
Supply Constraints Across Key Components
Management cautioned that demand is outstripping supply, leaving Dell constrained on critical components, especially DRAM and NAND. Additional bottlenecks include CPUs, disk drives, leading- and mature-node products, ABF substrate, T-Glass and optical parts, all of which could limit near-term shipment upside.
Customer Orders Delayed by Product Availability
Some large customers want products faster than Dell can currently deliver, leading to deferrals of certain purchases. In response, buyers are placing orders earlier to secure access to constrained supply, extending visibility but also highlighting the operational challenges of meeting AI-related demand.
While CSG remains profitable, Dell expects operating income rate to ease to about 6% in Q3, as it balances growth and share against pricing. Management also flagged a competitive PC landscape and noted that unit volumes are likely to be down in the second half, prompting ongoing price discovery.
Higher Variable Compensation Lifts Operating Expenses
Operating expenses increased 22% to $4 billion, with management attributing much of the rise to higher variable compensation tied to strong company performance. Even so, opex fell meaningfully as a percentage of revenue, reinforcing the underlying operating leverage of the model.
Pricing and Input-Cost Inflation in Infrastructure
Growth in traditional servers and storage includes a meaningful contribution from price increases as component costs move higher. Storage pricing in particular reflects higher material costs, especially NAND, suggesting that part of the revenue surge is driven by inflation in the supply chain.
Lightning Product Still Early in Commercial Cycle
Dell’s Lightning parallel file-system offering remains in an early commercialization phase, currently in beta with several customers. The product is in competitive runoffs, and management framed it as a strategic bet for high-performance AI and data workloads rather than a near-term revenue driver.
Management noted that more cost-sensitive customers are stretching PC upgrade timelines, resulting in a larger installed base of older devices. While commercial demand is healthy, these extended cycles could temper consumer growth and require continued product and pricing adjustments.
Robust Guidance Signals Confidence in AI Upside
For Q3, Dell guided to $49 billion in revenue at the midpoint, up roughly 80% year on year, with ISG up about 145% and AI server revenue at $19 billion. Full-year guidance calls for $192 billion in revenue, about 70% growth, EPS of $25.50, AI server revenue tripling to $74 billion and operating expenses held near 8% of revenue as operating income grows roughly 120%.
Dell’s earnings call painted the picture of a company firmly in the slipstream of the AI infrastructure boom, while still capitalizing on a steady PC recovery. Despite supply bottlenecks, margin normalization in CSG and rising input costs, management’s confidence and sharply raised guidance suggest investors are looking at a multi-year growth story rather than a fleeting spike in demand.

Dell AI Data Platform, the data foundation of the Dell AI Factory, expands with new data orchestration and storage capabilities
Unified Semantic Layer and Enterprise Knowledge Graph give every application and agent the same trusted view of enterprise data
Dell AI Data Platform shortens the wait between question and insight with accelerated data processing that processes data nearly 4 times faster on average than CPUs alone
Dell AI Data Platform storage enhancements improve security and benchmark performance

ROUND ROCK, Texas, October 06, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Dell Technologies (NYSE: DELL) expands the Dell AI Data Platform so AI systems deliver better answers, cost less to run and reach production faster, giving applications and agents trusted, current context from a company's own data.
In most cases the model isn't the bottleneck to achieving enterprise scale for AI. The data is. A company's most useful information sits in files, databases, cloud services and systems across multiple sites. Most of it was created long before anyone expected an AI agent to read it. It was never labeled, connected or organized with a machine reader in mind. As a result, agents burn tokens reconstructing answers that should already exist. Every query means more steps, more compute, more cost and slower, less trustworthy results.
The Dell AI Data Platform is built end to end, from where data is stored to where agents use it. Storage moves critical data to accelerated compute without bottlenecks; orchestration connects and prepares it; analytics and search transform and index it. NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models enable document parsing, embedding and reranking. NVIDIA cuVS accelerates vector indexing and search. Because every layer runs on one platform, everything it produces traces back to governed data the customer already owns. Agents return to the same documents, history and decisions repeatedly, and most systems rebuild their understanding from scratch every time. That means answering the same two questions on every request: what does this term mean and how does it relate to everything else? Dell is extending the Dell AI Data Platform with three new features to answer both at once.
The Unified Semantic Layer gives structured and unstructured information consistent business meaning with rules, definitions and a searchable glossary, so a term means the same thing everywhere it appears. If one system calls it a client and another calls it an account, AI now knows they're the same thing. Users can also import existing ontologies and classification taxonomies, reusing industry-standard or enterprise-specific taxonomy assets. Dell is also enabling NVIDIA Auto-Ontology, an open-source library that builds knowledge graphs from enterprise data, to extend the Unified Semantic Layer.
The Enterprise Knowledge Graph maps how structured and unstructured data is related, so an application or an agent can find the right context. It uses metadata, lineage and query history to keep tuning the graph as activity changes. When an agent asks a question, the platform pulls in every related piece it's allowed to see: the right tables, data products, multimodal data and vector indexes, wherever they live. For instance, a manufacturer chasing a production line problem can trace one odd sensor reading to the machine, its repair history, the supplier batch and the orders at risk.
Knowledge Agents put that context to work. Each one acts as a trusted advisor on a single topic, grounded in a defined slice of the Enterprise Knowledge Graph. Customers set the rules: what guidance it follows, what data it can see, what quality bar it must clear and how much it's allowed to spend. NVIDIA Nemotron Retriever models provide reasoning and visual understanding to Knowledge Agents.
The Unified Semantic Layer, Knowledge Graph and Knowledge Agents hold a customer's most valuable and sensitive information, so they stay inside the platform in the customer's data center. The platform builds context from that data, keeps it current as the business changes and shares it across every application and agent, without locking customers into any single model, data or storage provider.
Acceleration and security built into the data path
Business context is only reliable if data is accurate, current and governed from source to application. Customers should not have to adopt another proprietary layer to accelerate different parts of their data environment. Dell brings acceleration into the data engines themselves, working with NVIDIA across the data path. Data must be transformed and analyzed, then reach accelerated compute fast enough to keep GPUs saturated and stay protected along the way. Dell data and storage advancements include:
cuDF accelerated data processing with Apache Arrow: New testing shows that the Dell Data Processing Engine, powered by NVIDIA cuDF on NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, processes data nearly 4 times faster on average than CPUs alone across a range of workloads, and up to 20 times faster on batch processing workloads.¹ Apache Arrow moves data efficiently between Dell storage and processing, so jobs can query data in place. AI service providers and enterprises running shared AI platforms can serve more teams and customers from one cluster while keeping each tenant's data isolated and secure.
Benchmark workload performance: The new Dell Storage Performance Tool helps customers confidently size AI infrastructure, compare vendor solutions and keep GPUs fed by testing the performance of their S3-compatible object storage across training, inference and checkpointing.
Dell is expanding Dell AI Data Platform implementation services across its data and storage engines to move organizations from deployment to production results quickly and reliably. Dell Services establish a production-ready foundation, activating the platform's analytics, processing, search and orchestration capabilities while keeping the platform tuned to the demands of AI workloads.
Arthur Lewis, president, Infrastructure Solutions Group, Dell Technologies:
"Data without context is just noise. Most enterprises have spent years making their data accessible. That's not the same as making it usable. An agent that can find a customer record but doesn't know what it means, how it connects to everything else, or whether it can be trusted isn't intelligent. It's just fast. The companies that solve it won't just deploy AI faster or run more agents. They'll get more out of the data they already have."

Why Is Dell Technologies (DELL) Up 9.3% Since Last Earnings Report?

A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Dell Technologies (DELL). Shares have added about 9.3% in that time frame, outperforming the S&P 500.
Will the recent positive trend continue leading up to its next earnings release, or is Dell Technologies due for a pullback? Well, first let's take a quick look at its most recent earnings report in order to get a better handle on the recent drivers for Dell Technologies Inc. before we dive into how investors and analysts have reacted as of late.
DELL Q2 Earnings Beat Estimates, Strong AI Demand Aids Revenue Growth
Dell Technologies reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $7.04 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 41.65%. The company reported earnings of $2.32 per share in the year-ago quarter.
Revenues surged 58% to $46.97 billion and beat the consensus mark by 8.57%. Broad-based infrastructure demand drove the quarterly results, while AI server orders reached a record $60.9 billion.
DELL's ISG Growth Accelerates Across the Portfolio
Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) revenues jumped 89% year over year to a record $31.78 billion. AI-optimized server revenues doubled to $16.4 billion, while traditional servers and networking revenues surged 122% year over year to $10.53 billion. Dell exited the quarter with $95 billion of AI backlog, while its opportunity pipeline remained multiples of backlog.
Storage revenues increased 26% year over year to $4.85 billion as Dell IP demand grew above the market for a sixth consecutive quarter.
ISG operating income jumped 225% year over year to $4.78 billion, with operating margin expanding 620 basis points (bps) on a year-over-year basis to 15%. Dell also said its AI customer base surpassed 6,500 across neocloud, sovereign and enterprise customers.
Dell's Server Refresh Opportunity Supports Demand
Dell said traditional server demand reflects data-center modernization, security and resiliency requirements, and rising CPU needs tied to AI and agentic workloads. The company still has roughly 1.2 million installed assets running 14th-generation or older servers, leaving a sizable refresh opportunity as customers upgrade infrastructure.
Dell also highlighted significant consolidation benefits from newer systems. Seventeenth-generation servers can replace five to seven legacy servers, while 18th-generation systems can replace up to 13. The newer platforms also offer higher processing density and better power efficiency, supporting modernization even as industry supply remains constrained.

CSG operating income increased 42% year over year to $1.14 billion. The operating margin improved 120 bps to 7.6%, supported by pricing discipline and greater scale.
Dell said it will continue balancing demand with product availability as it pursues profitable share gains in the client business.

Non-GAAP gross margin rose 78% year over year to $9.93 billion, while the gross margin improved to 21.1% from 18.7%.
Non-GAAP operating expenses increased 22% year over year to $4 billion but fell to 8.5% of revenues from 11% a year earlier, reflecting meaningful operating leverage.

title: Jim Cramer Prefers Dell (DELL) But Calls HPE the Cheaper Stock. Here is the Gap
text: Skip to navigation Skip to main content Skip to right column Jim Cramer Prefers Dell (DELL) But Calls HPE the Cheaper Stock. Here is the Gap Tue, October 6, 2026 at 5:17 PM PDT 4 min read Dell Technologies Inc. (NYSE:DELL) was named the better operator of the two by Jim Cramer on Mad Money on October 6, in a segment that still called Hewlett Packard Enterprise the cheaper stock. Dell traded at around $573 on October 6, up 3.80% on the day, while Hewlett Packard Enterprise traded near $71. Cramer was precise about the trade-off. "I am not ready to say that I like HPE more than Dell because Dell's best of breed," he said, before adding that the other stock "acts a lot cheaper given the lower valuation." READ ALSO: Marvell vs. Broadcom: Which Custom AI Chip Stock Has More Room to Run? Jim Cramer Prefers Dell (DELL) But Calls HPE the Cheaper Stock. Here is the Gap The Gap Is in the Forward Multiple, Not the Trailing One: Cramer put Dell at "18 times" earnings.
